title: Cryptographic architecture & HSM onboarding — Aurora HealthTech security sync
summary: Customer is evaluating Redwood for hosting PHI-bearing inference workloads. Primary concerns: BYOK/HSM integration, key rotation & split-key policy, audit log fidelity, data residency, and SSO/RBAC. SE walked through envelope encryption, key wrapping, KMIP vs cloud KMS, and architecture options for private deployment with HSM. Next actions: share HSM onboarding guide, run a 2-week pilot with CloudHSM, provide SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, and schedule a hands-on key rotation tabletop with Aurora infra team.
topics: HSM providers and onboarding (CloudHSM, Thales, on-prem HSM)
Audit logs and key access traces
Key rotation, split-key, and escrow policies

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SecEng), Dr. Priya Nair (CISO, Aurora), Tom Browning (Infra), Salma Ahmed (Compliance), Victor Lee (Platform), Jenny Park (SecOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Discussed BYOK/HSM options, envelope encryption, audit logging cadence, and SOC2 artifacts. Action items listed.

00:00 Ethan: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we'll do a 60 to 80 minute deep dive on our cryptographic approach and hand off any materials at the end. maya and carlos from our security and se teams are here —
00:12 Priya: great, thanks. we have a few goals: confirm that keys can be customer-managed for PHI workloads, ensure we get sufficient audit logs for our auditors, and see how rotation and split-key could work.
00:25 Maya: yep, that's exactly what we'll cover. quick question — is Aurora planning on cloud HSM or an on-prem hardware module?
00:30 Tom: We're primarily cloud-first; leaning towards AWS CloudHSM in us-east-1 for latency and residency. but we do have a Thales vHSM plan for a secondary in eu-west-1.
00:42 Carlos: okay good, that maps to our supported patterns. high-level, Redwood supports three models: 1) Redwood-managed KMS (we manage keys in our KMS), 2) BYOK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS/CMEK where customer owns key in their cloud account), and 3) BYOK with customer HSM (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM integrated via KMIP or device connectors).
00:59 Priya: can you describe the envelope encryption flow end-to-end? like, where are master keys, how are data keys protected, and who can see plaintext?
01:12 Maya: sure. typical flow: model payloads and artifacts are encrypted with data keys (DEKs). DEKs are wrapped with a master key (KEK) that lives in the customer's HSM or cloud KMS depending on topology. Redwood stores only wrapped DEKs; plaintext never persists in our control plane. when a serving node needs to decrypt, it requests the KEK unwrap operation against the customer's KMS/HSM via a short-lived signed token — we support mutual TLS for that channel.
01:40 Victor: is the unwrap operation happening in our control plane or in the runtime GPUs? concerns around sensitive plaintext in memory on host vs GPU memory — we need to understand blast radius.
01:52 Maya: good call. we do unwrap just-in-time in a small trusted enclave in the serving runtime. the plaintext DEK lives only in process memory and is zeroed after the session; we support hardware-backed enclaves when available. for GPU memory, we use KV caching where possible — the cache is encrypted and flushed on pod termination.
02:12 Jenny: what about audit logs? auditors want key usage events at the operation and principal level (who used unwrap, from which host, timestamp, correlation id). does Redwood forward those events?
02:23 Carlos: yes. two sources: 1) the KMS/HSM audit trail (we don't duplicate tamper-proof logs from CloudHSM/AWS KMS) which you keep in your account; and 2) Redwood's runtime access logs which show request id, model, route, and which key material reference was used. we can stream those logs to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, or Splunk) with configurable retention. note: the KMS audit has the cryptographic operation provenance, the runtime logs provide application context.
02:56 Salma: auditors ask for immutable logs and proof that we can't alter KMS audit. how do you ensure we can present a chain of custody?
03:07 Carlos: for CloudHSM/AWS KMS, the provider certifies their audit trail and we recommend ingesting provider logs into your long-term archival in a write-once location (like WORM S3). Redwood's logs are append-only and signed; we can provide periodic signed snapshots for audit. we also support push of logs to your SOC tools in real time.
03:34 Tom: what's the network path when using BYOK/cloud HSM? e.g. do requests go from Redwood control plane to customer VPC, or do you deploy connectors in our VPC?
03:45 Maya: two options: 1) connector model — we run a small connector inside your VPC (we call it the KMS proxy) which handles KMIP/TLS to your HSM; it uses mTLS to talk back to Redwood control plane for auth and metrics. 2) direct cloud integration — if you're using AWS KMS in the same cloud account, Redwood can call the KMS API using cross-account IAM roles (we do assume-role with STS). connector model gives you network isolation and is preferred for private deployments.
04:12 Priya: connector model sounds better. who runs it and what's the attack surface?
04:18 Maya: the connector is customer-deployed; it's a container we provide. it restricts outbound egress to the HSM endpoints only, uses mutual TLS, and maintains a local cache only for session tokens (short TTL). it does not persist keys. we provide the image and the helm chart; our security team does a review and we can do an SCA scan with your team.
04:36 Victor: do you support KMIP? our Thales side is KMIP heavy and we want to use the same key lifecycle tools.
04:42 Carlos: yes KMIP is supported via the connector. we also support native CloudHSM APIs and AWS KMS via cross-account. for on-prem Thales, KMIP works fine but you will need to open ports and possibly set up a VPN or private link.
05:02 Priya: rotation — can we enforce automatic rotation policies from our KMS and have Redwood pick up the new key versions without downtime?
05:10 Maya: typical pattern: you rotate the KEK in your KMS; the wrapped DEKs remain valid until re-wrap. Redwood tracks key version metadata and supports key version discovery. we can do lazy re-wrap on access (first access after rotation will unwrap with the new KEK) or a bulk re-wrap job that we can run during a maintenance window. both patterns are supported.
05:35 Jenny: what about split-key or key escrow? auditors sometimes want split control so no single person can export the key.
05:42 Carlos: split-key is more an HSM/custodian feature — CloudHSM supports multi-ACL and separation. for split-key, you'd likely use an external KMS or an HSM cluster with dual-control for key import/export. Redwood's role is to respect the KMS policy and never hold plaintext KEKs; we can enforce policy-based deny of export operations.
06:05 Tom: are there any limitations with model serving, e.g., large models that require checkpoint encryption strategies?
06:12 Maya: for model checkpoints and artifacts, we use object storage encryption + envelope encryption. large artifacts are chunked and encrypted with DEKs, same wrapping as runtime. we also support on-the-fly streaming decryption to reduce memory pressure during loads.
06:29 Priya: I'd like to understand the threat model — if Redwood's control plane is compromised, can an attacker decrypt data?
06:36 Carlos: assuming you're on BYOK with keys in your AWS account and CloudHSM, the attacker would need access to your KEK in your account. Redwood stores wrapped DEKs; the ability to unwrap requires an unwrapping call to your KMS/HSM and the connector credentials. we recommend hardening the connector, enforce least privilege IAM, restrict STS assume-role to specific source IPs, and enable VPC endpoints and PrivateLink. also enable KMS IAM conditions (e.g., aws:SourceIp and aws:ViaAWSService constraints) and use separate service principals for read-only operations.
07:12 Victor: can Redwood's runtime perform operations without contacting KMS each call — i.e., can you cache DEKs to avoid per-request latency? what's the TTL and how do we revoke?
07:23 Maya: we do prefix caching and DEK caching for performance; TTL is configurable — typical default is 5 minutes for inference workloads. you can elect to set very short TTLs for high-security needs. if you need immediate revocation, we recommend rotating the KEK or issuing a deny policy in the KMS which causes unwraps to fail; Redwood also supports an administrative revoke that clears runtime caches via our control plane and triggers immediate evictions.
07:52 Priya: legal question — data residency. we need keys and data to remain in the same region (US-only). can Redwood pin the serving region and KMS locality?
08:04 Maya: yes. for Dedicated and Private customers we allow region pinning. for BYOK with CloudHSM, the HSM cluster must be in the same region as your data; we will route requests to that region. we also offer private deployments (VPC/offline) if you need fully isolated control plane.
08:22 Tom: SSO and RBAC — how granular can you get? we need separation between platform ops and security admins, and no single person should be able to both create key material and change RBAC.
08:33 Carlos: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 / OIDC for SSO and fine-grained RBAC at the org, project, and route level. we can map groups from your IdP to roles. also recommend enabling MFA for administrative principals. we support audit trails for admin operations (role changes, key rotations triggered from Redwood console).
08:58 Salma: auditors also ask for proof of dual-control and documented change approval workflows. can you integrate approvals into the console?
09:06 Lina: yes, we have an approvals workflow for sensitive operations — you can require N-of-M approvers for actions like changing KMS connectors, enabling export, or deleting key references. that creates an auditable chain inside Redwood.
09:22 Priya: what about HSM onboarding lifecycle — import of existing key material? we have existing wrapped keys and a vendor-managed HSM; we'd prefer not to re-key everything if possible.
09:31 Maya: we support both import of wrapped key material and re-wrap migrations. if keys are in a vendor HSM you can perform a secure export into a wrapped format we accept (e.g., PKCS#11 wrapped or KMIP wrapped) and then import into your CloudHSM cluster or keep it in the vendor HSM and point connector to it. the import process uses a split-offline transfer and we recommend a joint runbook.
09:58 Victor: are there any performance implications for calling remote KMS frequently, especially for high-throughput scoring?
10:06 Maya: there is extra latency on initial unwraps; that's why we cache DEKs and suggest batching and prefix caching. for high-throughput, best practice is to use a DEK-per-shard model with a short-lived cache on the runtime nodes; that reduces KMS calls dramatically. we can help size your cache TTLs during the pilot.
closing_notes: Wrap-up: customer to review compliance doc list; Redwood to run pilot using CloudHSM connector in us-east-1. Follow-up meeting to be scheduled for key rotation tabletop the week of 2025-04-21. Pricing/pilot details to be emailed by Ethan.
